pyproject.toml: # Correctness and security rules only; style is not a CI gate.
select = ["E9", "F", "B", "S", "PLE", "W605", "PGH004"]   # PGH004: a noqa must name its rule
"B011",  # assert False in tests is deliberate
"S311",  # random is used for seeded fuzzing, never for secrets
"B904",  # explicit `raise ... from None` is used where chaining would leak
"B007",  # historical benchmark scripts keep their loop variables
"live_capture.py" = ["S603", "S404", "S607"]   # argv-only subprocess with resolved executable, reviewed
"tools/check_pin_drift.py" = ["S603"]       # resolved git executable with argv-only arguments, reviewed
"tools/check_release_exposure.py" = ["S603"]   # resolved git executable with argv-only arguments, reviewed
"tools/check_workflow_policy.py" = ["S603"]    # resolved git executable with argv-only arguments, reviewed
"tools/build_manifest.py" = ["S603", "S607"]  # fixed argv `git rev-parse` for manifest provenance only
# Presentation application (stage 1a): argv-only subprocess calls, no shell. The workers run sys.executable on the
# app's own scripts; tcpdump comes from live_capture.capture_command, which validates interface and filter.
"presentation/launch.py" = ["S603", "S310"]   # S310: urlopen only of http://127.0.0.1:<port> built in main()

#   B404 import subprocess, B603 subprocess call without shell — live_capture.py

.gitleaks.toml: # gitleaks configuration (SSDLC.md): extend the default rules, allow documented protocol test vectors.
# The default condition (OR: a path or a regex) and target (the secret) are those of the deprecated [allowlist]
# table this replaced; gitleaks 8.30 refuses [allowlist] alongside [[allowlists]].
description = "Published protocol test vectors are not credentials"
# RFC 6455 section 1.3 WebSocket example nonce/accept and RFC 9001/9369 QUIC vectors reproduced in fixtures.
# The SSH post-quantum key exchange name in the PROTOCOLS.md v0.58 table ("key exchange names:
# sntrup761x25519") matches generic-api-key; exact token only, so a real key next to it still flags.
# Go table tests carry synthetic HTTP/1 messages as hex (go/internal/protocols/textroute/boundary_test.go on
# claude/mutation-gremlins 296227b, PRO-126); a case name ending in "key ..." or "tokens" next to the hex reads as
# key=value to generic-api-key. Allowed only when BOTH hold (SEC-CI-1, PRO-183/PRO-184): the file is a Go test under
# go/, and the secret is all hex decoding to an HTTP/1 start line ("GET ", "POST ", "HTTP/1."). The same hex in any
# other file, which could be a captured request carrying a cookie or bearer token, still flags
description = "Synthetic hex-encoded HTTP/1 messages in Go table tests are not credentials"
# App Research live rounds (research/live-results-YYYY-MM-DD-rN.tsv, PRO-145/PRO-153) record each name's public DNS
# CNAME chain as "host>host>..." (r5 line 8, 655d440/75695d3, was the first; its one-off exact entry is replaced
# by this rule). generic-api-key reads a label such as "edgekey" before ">" as key=value and flags
# the next hostname. This allowlist applies only when BOTH hold: the file is a live-results TSV, and the whole
# match is a chain of lowercase dot-separated DNS names joined by ">". A key, token or password in the same file
# is not such a chain, so it still flags (tools/check_gitleaks_allowlist.py, negative controls).
description = "Public DNS CNAME chains in App Research live-results TSVs are not credentials"
# Stage 8 (A16/A10): an NSS key log (SSLKEYLOGFILE) must never be committed. Secrets and client randoms are
# 32 or 48 bytes of hex; placeholder vectors in tests are all-zero or repeated bytes and are allowlisted by
# the paths above only when they are such placeholders (tools/check_no_keylogs.py enforces that part).
description = "TLS key-log line (CLIENT_RANDOM / TRAFFIC_SECRET with hex secrets)"
tools/golint/golangci.yml: # golangci-lint configuration for the Go engine (go/), run by tools/go_lint.py in the `go-lint` ci job.
# Locked by rule 16 (tools/scanner_config.lock.json): loosening a linter, a setting or an exclusion means
# advancing a reviewed baseline. golangci-lint is given this file with --config; a .golangci.* file anywhere
# in the tree is refused by the workflow policy, so no other configuration can load on its own.
timeout: 10m            # the analysis budget; the job's own timeout is above it
tests: true             # _test.go files are linted too
relative-path-mode: wd  # paths relative to go/, as the baseline records them
- bodyclose           # HTTP response bodies not closed
- unconvert           # conversions to the same type (hide a type change at the call site)
# suppression hygiene: a nolint directive must name its linter and say why (no blanket nolint)
# staticcheck and gosec run as their own pinned tools (tools/go_lint.py), with their full check sets.
# Writes to the CLI's stdout/stderr and to report writers: a failed write there has no recovery, and the
# buffered writer's Flush or Close, which surfaces it, stays checked.
max-issues-per-linter: 0   # report everything: the baseline compares complete sets

"OSV id (or an alias), the lockfile and package it applies to, why the risk is accepted, and when it",
"expires (at most 90 days ahead). An expired entry, or one that matches no finding, fails the job."

"reason": "rardecode 2.1.0: unrestricted RAR dictionary sizes allow a denial of service (CVE-2025-11579). It is in the CI-only gitleaks 8.30.1 build, never shipped, and the secret scan reads git history, not RAR archives; govulncheck -mode=binary over the built gitleaks finds no call to the vulnerable symbols (toolchain-audit job, every run). The fix, rardecode 2.2.0, does not build with gitleaks' mholt/archives 0.1.2, so it waits for a gitleaks release that moves archives forward (PRO-128).",
tools/golint/gosec/go.mod: // gosec v2.29.0's rules. Its own golang.org/x/tools (v0.49.0) cannot read Go 1.27 export data, so every package
// fails to load and gosec reports 0 issues; x/tools is raised below to v0.52.0 (the loader golangci-lint uses).
// tools/go_lint.py fails on any gosec load error, so a loader regression cannot pass as an all-clear.
